html:
The most celebrated poet of Siam, born in Bangkok four years after the founding of the Rattanakosin Kingdom. His best known work is the long verse tale Phra Aphai Mani.

Sunthorn Phu rose as a court poet under King Rama II, who loved poetry and helped him with royal works. After the king's death in 1824 he lost favour with the new king, Rama III, and spent close to twenty years as a Buddhist monk, wandering the country. Late in life he found new patrons, among them the prince who became Pinklao, second king under Rama IV.

He wrote in a lively, plain style that ordinary people could enjoy. His nirat, poems of journeys, mix travel with longing and personal feeling. Phra Aphai Mani is a fantasy of a prince whose magic flute puts enemies to sleep, with mermaids, ogres and foreign ships, and it shows a Siam aware of the wider world. In 1986, on the 200th anniversary of his birth, UNESCO honoured him as a great figure of world literature. See Siam, then Thailand.
